lede: One name threaded through nearly every feed today: Jensen Huang. News that Nvidia is investigating its chief executive's links to a suspected Chinese spy ran on the AI news wire and surfaced on Lemmy, while Huang himself drew 733,363 views on Wikipedia, third behind Russell Brand at 1,010,049, and spawned Polymarket contracts on whether he leaves by year end. Away from that story, a magnitude 5.4 earthquake struck near the Tanimbar Islands in Indonesia, and the third India versus New Zealand one-day cricket match was the top Google search.

throughlines.title: Nvidia Launches Probe Into CEO Huang Links To Suspected Chinese Spy
throughlines.gist: An AI news wire and Lemmy both carried Nvidia's investigation into its chief executive, a story that crossed from the tech press into social feeds on the same day.

throughlines.title: Jensen Huang
throughlines.gist: The same executive also topped the charts as a person, drawing a Wikipedia surge and Polymarket bets on whether he resigns or divorces before year end.

throughlines.title: Horible public key tricks
throughlines.gist: A public-key puzzle drew developers on both Hacker News and Stack Overflow, the day's one thread where two technical sites were chewing on the same cryptography problem.
